#Fees must Fall

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Summary:
Across the country University Students are protesting the 10% increase in University Tuition fees. Wits University students were the first to come out preventing staff and students from attending lectures and eventually preventing staff from leaving the campus. On Monday UCT students joined the call of “Fees must fall” picking up on the slogan Rhodes must fall the student protest that brought Universities to a standstill earlier this year when students called for the transformation of Universities.
On Monday Rhodes University, and Stellenbosch joined WITS and UCT. By the end of Tuesday campuses across the country had come out including Tuks, and CUPT. Today Universities across the country have come to a standstill. Students have been protesting the increase of fees for several years now but this is the first time they have all come out at the same time across the country.
State and Private funding of Universities has been decreasing over the years and poor Students and their parents are taking the brunt of the financial stress. Many students are not poor enough to get state subsidies and their parents take out loans and bursaries to pay for their fees but there is little left for living cost, transport and food making the student’s lives extremely stressful. Students are graduating with massive loans to repay. Others who have qualified and got a degree don’t get their certificate because the university withholds the awarding of a degree until fees are paid up. This insert will focus on these students and their stories with the backdrop of the last weeks drama of students and University administrations coming head to head.


Further information:
Universities have been put under pressure to transform and admit more students and create access for students that would have previously been prohibited from attending them because of high tuition fees. The Universities have largely done this by creating Financial Aid Schemes but the demand has outstripped the resources.
Universities fund themselves from 3 sources, student fees, state subsidies and thirdly private enterprise. With the dramatic increase of poorer students the income from fees has fallen and driven the need to increase fees. The State has consistently under subsidised Universities something that began under Apartheid when Universities were challenging the State. However the Government continues to put the Universities under pressure to create access and complains that fees are too high but has not increased its funding. The State subsidy The National Student Financial Aid Scheme has not increased at the same rate as the increase of students. Private Enterprise tends to do vanity funding and doesn’t pay for the hard running costs like administrative staff, rates, taxes, electricity and maintenance, student transport etc.
As a result universities have been forced to increase the class size in an attempt to increase their fees base, but have not had the funds to increase the number of staff or the teaching resources or the infra-structure. As a result teaching standards have dropped, there is a larger failure rate and research is underfunded.

Press Release:


Student Protests
It’s been dubbed one of the biggest student protests since 1976 and, as more universities across the country join the call that “Fees must fall”, momentum is growing. In just ten days, thousands of students from many of the country’s most elite institutions have brought the corridors of learning to a standstill. Carte Blanche asks: Is higher education a right, or a privilege for a select few?


Script:


Script: 1000 of students marched on the Union Building on Friday afternoon demanding that the president address their call for a zero increase in university fees. After a week of protest came the announcement they had been waiting for
Zuma “We agreed that there will be a zero increase of university fees in 2016
Script ”But this was on national television, not to the assembled students. They were outraged having waited for hours to see the president. It enflamed the already volatile mood and what followed were pitched battles. Two police cars were burnt and shops looted.
Upsound
Script: This comes after a week filled with shocking scenes around the # Fees must fall campaign. Students across the country have stood together in a way we haven’t seen since the 1980s. The protest has raged from Wits University, to Rhodes to the gates of Parliament to the Union Buildings. People are talking about an African Spring, a tipping point in the history of South Africa.
Mothheo Lengoasa: “Our own Ministers who are in suits who were in the 1976 but are in suits now who can’t speak to us as students and they were in the same position…. Its hurtful to think this is 20 years after democracy and we are supposed to be a free country …we are not being listened to we have to be animalistic before we are listened to.
Script: Workers and students united their struggle garnering support across racial lines.
LINK: “Initially the Fees must fall campaign played out on University campuses but on Wednesday students took their concerns directly to parliament. It was the first time that the gates of the National assembly had been stormed. “
Upsound More conflict shots
Script: It was a bizarre scene, while stun grenades exploded outside parliament Minister of finance Nhlanhla Nene carried on delivering the interim budget- it was business as usual says analyst Judith February
Judith February “This is what happens when a government which seems to me to be increasingly A out of touch and B also where there is a serial lack of accountability. People are tired of them not listening
Script “The EFF were the only parliamentary members outside that afternoon having once again been removed from the chamber
Floyd “They are the ones who have been promising free education since 1994 and they are not giving it now what kind of liberation is this if you aren’t going to give people access to education?”
LINK: 06 14 23 05 Amidst the chaos of exploding stun grenades it was hard not to be moved by the students singing the National anthem as their rallying cry.
Upsound
Script: And the irony when the children of struggle stalwarts like Kgotsi Chikane, son of Frank Chikane were dragged off and initially charged with treason.
UPsound’ All I want is to speak to Blade- that’s all we want talk to Blade
Script: # Fees must Fall has united students and those who can afford the increases stood in solidarity with those who can’t. Kevin French, father of a UCT student, was part of the crowd and was also violently arrested, and charged with treason
Upsound Kevin French ”Viva”
Script: Bridget Pitt, a Struggle activist from the 1980’s and parent of a protesting student says the dejavu was uncanny:
Bridget” The response at parliament yesterday seemed totally disproportionate. What they should have done is invite some of the students in to address parliament “
Script: Vice Chancellors find themselves in an ironic position. Many of them are former student activists and warned about this crisis years ago. But they face the task of delivering quality education amid spiralling inflation and exchange rates, and falling State subsidies. Wits Vice Chancellor Adam Habib wants students to understand what the consequences of the zero fees increase would mean:
Adam Habib “Under these conditions how do we balance the books. I can say I am going to cut the academic programs but then I am going to compromise the quality of education…I think poor students are absolutely entitled to a world class education as much as all other students are
Script: The protest started at Wits but was quickly mobilised through social media. UCT students blockaded Campus early Monday morning preventing 300 students from writing exams and causing kilometres of traffic build up on the highway. It took the administration by surprise as the SRC had already agreed to a 10.5% increase. But things turned nasty on Monday night when police acting on an interdict removed students from the administration building. Arresting 23 students and bringing hundreds more out it protest the next morning
Mbali Matandela “Its students coming from various progressive organizations…..coming together with non- partisan politics because party politics always divides. Yesterday when we were in jail the white students created a human shield in front of the police so they are willing to put their bodies on the line in front of black students
Script: By Tuesday afternoon all the country’s institutions of Higher learning were protesting. Another urgent meeting between Vice Chancellors and Minister of Higher Education and Training Blade Nzimande announced a compromise of a 6% inflation linked increase for 2016. That bought time to set up a task team to find a solution for the future
Blade ”The total amount of money collected from student fees in the system is 22 billion Rand, so if you say zero percent increase, it is 22 billion rand wiped off the system. I don’t believe the system would be able to afford that, much as we do not like the fact that we collect money from poor students, that’s why government has got the National Student Financial Aid Scheme to support the students
Script: Government subsidies for students have increased since 2008’s from 2,5 Billion to 9 Billion this year, but in real terms over the last 21 years government funding has been declining
Blabe “ From 1994 we have doubled, just more than doubled the number of university students but of course, funding for the core activities of the universities, as well as funding for infrastructure, and student accommodation has lagged behind
Script: Vice Chancellor of UCT Max Price says this has been a long time coming
John “Do you feel left in the lurch by the government after all this has been an issue that been around for some time now”
Max Price” There was a big National meeting in October 2014 around the funding of financial Aid. Many campuses have experienced protests at the start of each year when students can’t get back onto campus because they can’t pay their fees. ….Its actually been in the focus for a long time what the frustration is that there hasn’t been any action, ..the budget has not recognised that problem
Script: Students have tried hard to keep things under control but tempers have flared when those who wanted to stay out of the fray got sucked in. At Fort Hare and CPUT violence and looting got out of hand. Student leader Athabile Nonxuba has worked hard to keep students disciplined at UCT.
Athabile Nonxuba” 06 20 18 02 The leaders of this country have disconnected with the source which is the people they are claiming to be leading you cannot disconnect from the constituents if you want to know the narrative to the pain of the constituents but now Blade Nzimande has found comfort for himself. Then he has the audacity to tell us this is not a crisis and you are trying to make this a crisis.
Script: On Wednesday President Zuma slipped out the side entrance of parliament while the students railed against the gates calling for Minister Blade Nzimande to address them.
Link: After the chaos of the day before protest action gave way to legal action both here at the high court in Cape Town and down the road at the magistrate’s court.
Script: # Fees Must Fall students brought an urgent interdict against police for brutality. 6 students were detained and charged, 28 others had their charges dropped and were released
Bridget “the government’s response more and more is a kind of reactionary response, a response of silencing protest rather than addressing the issues. The fact that they have charged 6 students with high treason which I find absolutely extraordinary this is exactly the kind of tactic that were resorted to before
Max” We are balancing two things we want to say we support your goal and we are united with you we don’t support your methods we don’t think you should impose on other students to write exams …if they would have a form of protest that doesn’t impact other people’s rights there would be no conflict
Link; Well its about 24 hours since the chaos erupted at Parliament and the students have called an assembly here at UCT and while the violence has disappeared some of the rhetoric here is just as strong
Script” Vice Chancellor Max Price faced the wrath of the students for allowing police to arrest them on campus. Academic staff marched with students condemning the police presence. Deputy Dean of Health Sciences Reno Morar addressed the protestors
Upsound “As the academic staff we stand by our students and totally condemn the violence action of the police”
Script: Ironically Max Price son Illan was arrested the night before outside parliament. He committed to postponing exams for a week and to do everything in his power to get the charges dropped against the students arrested on campus.
Athabile “After apartheid for the first time Chumani Maxwele and 6 students were charged with treason this is the same charge for Sobukwe, Sobukwe was charged with treason, Mandela was charged for treason, now they have to reimagine what does it mean in 2015
Script: The # Fees must fall movement has won the battle for a zero increase in tuition fees for 2016 but is this a tipping point?
Judith February” It is far too early to say because I think that there are divisions within the student movement that is typical of these sorts of movements also between the universities and the way student leadership is doing politics “
Script: Students have sacrificed an enormous amount coming out in protest at this time of the year.
Adam Habib” 08 02 39 The fact that we are heading for exams in 12 days my students are meant to be writing exams I do not want them to lose this year, losing this year would mean that they would have to come back again and it reinforces the very problem we are talking about

On Monday Rhodes University, and Stellenbosch joined WITS and UCT. By the end of Tuesday campuses across the country had come out including Tuks, and CUPT. Today Universities across the country have come to a standstill. Students have been protesting the increase of fees for several years now but this is the first time they have all come out at the same time across the country. State and Private funding of Universities has been decreasing over the years and poor Students and their parents are taking the brunt of the financial stress. Many students are not poor enough to get state subsidies and their parents take out loans and bursaries to pay for their fees but there is little left for living cost, transport and food making the student’s lives extremely stressful. Students are graduating with massive loans to repay. Others who have qualified and got a degree don’t get their certificate because the university withholds the awarding of a degree until fees are paid up. This insert will focus on these students and their stories with the backdrop of the last weeks drama of students and University administrations coming head to head.
metadata.Further information: Universities have been put under pressure to transform and admit more students and create access for students that would have previously been prohibited from attending them because of high tuition fees. The Universities have largely done this by creating Financial Aid Schemes but the demand has outstripped the resources. Universities fund themselves from 3 sources, student fees, state subsidies and thirdly private enterprise. With the dramatic increase of poorer students the income from fees has fallen and driven the need to increase fees. The State has consistently under subsidised Universities something that began under Apartheid when Universities were challenging the State. However the Government continues to put the Universities under pressure to create access and complains that fees are too high but has not increased its funding. The State subsidy The National Student Financial Aid Scheme has not increased at the same rate as the increase of students. Private Enterprise tends to do vanity funding and doesn’t pay for the hard running costs like administrative staff, rates, taxes, electricity and maintenance, student transport etc. As a result universities have been forced to increase the class size in an attempt to increase their fees base, but have not had the funds to increase the number of staff or the teaching resources or the infra-structure. As a result teaching standards have dropped, there is a larger failure rate and research is underfunded.
